title: Swipe between story board columns on mobile

intentCoverage.report:
**Verdict: Caught.** The maintained phone indicator journey catches removal of accessible neighboring-column names after the observed Backlog → Taken swipe.

**Next proof action:** Retain the existing focused indicator journey as the gate for this promise. No repair is indicated by this single fault check; broader coverage remains outside this result.

The source is [SEED-373#swipe-between-story-board-columns](/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough/.worktrees/swipe-between-story-board-columns-on-mobile/.planning/seeds/SEED-373-swipe-between-story-board-columns.md), with [slice plan 640](/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough/.worktrees/swipe-between-story-board-columns-on-mobile/.planning/slice-plans/640-swipe-between-story-board-columns/PLAN.md), evaluated at `389627535ef9fc9ec5bf0809508c4c377b0d18e9`. The selected promise is that compact phone indicators preserve complete accessible neighboring-column names/counts, including after navigation (SRC-16/SRC-17). The caller’s suggested promise, fault and command held against this revision; no consequential target change was needed.

An owned detached scratch checkout used Node 24.21.0 and its own `npm ci --ignore-scripts` dependencies. Pre-probe tracked/untracked state was clean. The single fault added `display: none` to the coarse-pointer `.column-paging-control-label` rule at `dashboard/src/board.css:124`, replacing only the label’s accessible availability while retaining its DOM text, chevron, button and fixtures. Maintained assertions and fixture files were unchanged.

The same maintained command ran before, during and after the fault, with only the private proof-record path changing:

```sh
OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_FRONTEND_PROOF_RECORD=<phase-proof.json> caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard:frontend -- board-indicators.spec.ts --workers=1
```

- Baseline: both selected cases passed; strict verdict passed.
- Faulted: the first case’s native left swipe reached Taken (`--leftmost: 1` in the retained trace). Its call to `expectColumnReading` at `board-indicators.spec.ts:24` failed in the earlier `expectView` assertion at `dashboard/tests/boardPage.ts:47`: `expect(columnPagingControls(page)).toHaveText([...controls])`. The accessible-name role locator resolved to zero elements, receiving `[]` instead of `['Backlog 2 entries', 'Recently done 0 entries']`. This is the actual catch. The second case timed out in its name-based focus operation; that later block adds no separate assertion verdict.
- Independent wrong-behavior observation: a disposable standalone browser observer served a separately built actual frontend with the same service-boundary substitutes at 390×844 with native touch. Chromium `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree` and independent ARIA snapshots showed `Taken 1 entry` before the baseline swipe and `Backlog 2 entries`/`Recently done 0 entries` afterward. Under the fault, the buttons remained present with empty AX names before and after the same native swipe; the DOM retained those text strings while label display was `none`. This confirms the intended accessibility behavior broke, independently of the maintained locator failure.
- Restoration: a trapped cleanup restored the exact original CSS bytes. Original/restored SHA-256 matched (`828a2db7a20c5fe6bf44a309dcc5ff141ddd986a9163072f5cd01b5ed24d440c`), both restored cases strictly passed, and before/after Git states matched the clean pre-probe state. The owned scratch worktree was then removed and its deregistration verified. No primary checkout edits were made.

The Mac was awake on AC, using `caffeinate -s -i`, with 56% free memory and natural load 6.53 before setup / 4.09 before the fault / 5.64 afterward. One worker kept the selected proof bounded amid other development work. The shared [failure policy](/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough/.worktrees/swipe-between-story-board-columns-on-mobile/Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/references/failure-policy.md) remained applicable; deliberate fault failures were followed by restoration and a passing rerun. The standalone observer’s initial Node strip-only import failure was corrected with `--experimental-transform-types` before fault injection.

Prior disposition: slice 2 already owned this accessible-name proof; this result confirms that existing responsibility. No new repair or backlog decision was made.

Evidence remains in [/tmp/dough-intent-SEED-373.iRkXsf](/tmp/dough-intent-SEED-373.iRkXsf): `baseline-proof.json`, `faulted-proof.json`, `restored-proof.json`, `fault.diff`, `baseline-accessibility.json`, `faulted-accessibility.json`, `faulted-artifacts/` (traces and error contexts), `evidence-summary.json`, and `cleanup.json`.
